title: Release priming cohorts and anchor strategies (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
This is a personal scratchpad for the next model rollout (v2026-03-anchor). Focus is on traffic priming (seeding cohorts), version anchoring/pinning heuristics, and practical warmup to avoid cold-kv and cache-induced latency spikes. Not a runbook yet — more a capture of ideas, checks, and unresolved questions before I transform into the formal playbook.

High-level goals:
- Ramp new model variant (v2026-03-anchor) to production with minimal user-facing regressions and predictable unit-cost behavior.
- Make the first 30 minutes stable: avoid p95 spikes from cold KV/cache, avoid tail regressions in quality.
- Have clear, automatable escape hatches and one-button rollback.

Constraints / context:
- Dedicated pool in us-west with mixed traffic (hosted + dedicated customers).
- Warm-up window limited (we do not have capacity to pre-warm for > 6 hours).
- Downstream billing/observability: token-level cost metrics lag ~3m, trace samples are good for 1% of traffic.

Quick notes to self:
- Prioritize cohorts that exercise short- and long-context paths (30% short chat, 40% single-turn generation, 30% long context/streaming).
- Prefill KV cache using synthetic prefix list (see step below).
- Anchor pin strategy: soft-pin for first 8 hours (route new session creations to new variant; existing sessions remain on old variant).

Seeding / priming plan (ordered):
1) Preflight (T minus 60m):
   - Ensure model artifacts distributed to all nodes (check node_manifest).
   - Start synthetic warmup traffic from warmup workers (small requests that exercise kv and attn).
   - Kick off background cold-cache prefill: 10k unique prefixes across typical lengths (1k short, 6k medium, 3k long) at low concurrency.
   - Verify node-level KV hit-rate > 85% before moving.

2) Soft-seed (T minus 15m to T + 10m):
   - Route 0.5% of real traffic (by user cohort) to anchored variant. Use client-affinity hashing to keep traffic stable.
   - Monitor p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, and quality regression probes (sanity eval set of 200 prompts).

3) Ramp (T + 10m onward):
   - 0.5% -> 2% after 10m if no alerts.
   - 2% -> 8% after 20m.
   - 8% -> 25% after 30–60m if metrics stable.
   - After 4h, consider 50% if long-term metrics OK.

Cohort definitions (for seeding):
- Canary dev clients: internal SDK users, dev flag = true (captures heavy debug paths).
- Warmup cohort: small set of internal test accounts that run scripted sequences (deterministic).
- Edge-mimic cohort: sampled top-100 customers but routed only 0.2% of their sessions (to preserve consistency).
- New-session-only cohort: any session that creates a new conversation ID. Important for session-affinity pinning.

Anchoring / pinning heuristics:
- Soft pin: new sessions are encouraged to land on the new variant; existing conversation IDs remain on stable model for 8h by default.
- Hard pin window: allow product to set override where certain cohorts are fully pinned to new variant (A/B).
- Auto-eviction: if a conversation experiences >1.5x latency vs baseline for >3 requests, migrate that conversation back to stable (telemetry + migration API).

Telemetry / success metrics (primary):
- Latency: p95 <= baseline_p95 * 1.15 (soft threshold) and absolute p95 < 300ms for interactive tiers.
- Errors: 5xx < 0.2% and total error rate < baseline + 0.1%.
- Cost delta: token-cost-per-1k <= baseline * 1.25 (flag if >25% increase).
- Quality: automated eval set pass-rate (fuzzy-match) >= baseline - 1.5%. Also sample human eval if disparity.

Telemetry / guardrails (automated triggers):
- Immediate rollback triggers (automatic):
  - Spike in 5xx to >1% sustained for 5m.
  - p95 > baseline*1.5 sustained for 5m.
  - Eval set drift > 5% absolute (safety bound).
- Alert-only triggers (ops paged):
  - Cost delta > 30% for sustained 10m.
  - Slow increase in failure types (new exception signatures).

Warmup & cache prefill recipe (practical steps):
- Step 0: Build prefix corpus (use last 7 days of anonymized short/medium/long prompts). Strip PII.
- Step 1: Lightweight clients issue prefixes with concurrency floor=50, qps=200 for 20m. Spread across regions.
- Step 2: After warmup, run query with typical session flows (call with tool invokes, streaming) to exercise code paths.
- Step 3: Validate KV hit rate and model perf on warmup nodes.

Operational checklist (pre-launch quick run):
- [ ] Infra: node_manifest OK, all nodes have model artifact + checksum verified.
- [ ] SRE: routing rules staged and tested in canary cluster.
- [ ] Observability: dashboards created and pinned (latency, errors, tokens, cost).
- [ ] CS: top-10 customers notified of potential short window.
- [ ] Rollback: one-click rollback tested in staging and has been exercised once.
- [ ] Pager: on-call + model owner in rotation for first 4 hours.

Rollback & escape hatch design:
- Fast rollback: global traffic re-point to previous variant via routing control (expected <60s to fully propagate).
- Conversation-level migration: use session-migration API to move one session to stable if problematic.
- Quarantine: if particular client causes issues, divert their traffic to stable or throttle.

Post-launch activities:
- 30m check-in: quick triage (ops + model owner) to validate metrics and open issues.
- 4h review: decide on larger ramp or pause.
- 24h deep-dive: quality evals (human-in-the-loop), cold-start regressions review, and cost analysis.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we automate prefix corpus generation without exposing PII? (ask privacy team)
- How tolerant is billing pipeline to sudden token-cost spikes (lead time)? (finance)
- Need a deterministic small eval harness that runs in <90s and gives us a quality score we can act on automatically.
- Decide whether to include dedicated clients in initial 8h soft-pin (pros: realistic, cons: risky).

Quick reference commands (notes):
- Check node distribution: infractl model status --model v2026-03-anchor --region us-west
- Kick warmup job: infractl warmup run --model v2026-03-anchor --corpus warmup-prefix-20260301 --concurrency 50 --duration 20m
- Toggle route: routingctl set-weight --variant v2026-03-anchor --weight 0.005 --scope global

Notes to self (end):
- Keep this doc alive during launch and fold the parts that worked into the formal runbook.
- Save snapshots of dashboards at each step (use /dashshots/ channel).
- After rollout, write a short postmortem-style note with top 3 surprises (latency, quality drift, cost).

-- Gina
